carbon_policy_signal.item: German nuclear capacity addition (Moscow-linked northwest project) regulatory approval eases power demand; reduces marginal gas-dispatch generation and DA spread pressure.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Lower gas-marginal generation dispatch reduces thermal emissions and EUA demand; DA curve shape flattens, diminishing fuel-switch economics and EUA floor support from power upside.

freshness_caveat: Coal (210d stale, as of 2025-12-26) and clean dark (205d stale, as of 2025-12-31) data are outdated. Current directional bias (coal 7th pctile) may not reflect recent moves; use for context only. TTF, GB Power, DE Power, storage, renewable share, and EUA current as of 2026-07-24 / 2026-07-23 (0–1 days old).
risk_flags: GB power at 98th pctile (155 EUR/MWh, +5.8% daily) signals acute supply-demand imbalance; winter peak risk asymmetric to upside.
EU storage 15.7pp below seasonal (54.6% full, 28th pctile) — refill pace under stress if TTF elevated and LNG diverted by Hormuz premium.
Coal at 7th pctile (96 USD/t, 210 days stale); clean dark spread 48th pctile. Gas-to-coal margin supports sustained generation, but refill pressure offsets.
Hormuz escalation + Middle East violence pricing into LNG spot; EU sanctions resolution may unlock Russian flows to third countries, shifting global LNG arb and TTF flow dynamics.

base.summary: GB supply tensions persist; TTF holds elevated on storage deficit and LNG arb. DA soft from renewables; Q4 power tracks storage refill pace.

downside.summary: Middle East de-escalates; EU sanctions clear Russian supply channels; LNG arb reverses. GB wind normalizes; renewable share falls; demand softens; storage refill eases.

upside.summary: Hormuz escalates or Strait transits disrupted. Asian LNG spot surges; EU refill costs spike; storage premium reasserts. GB wind output falters.

themes: GB power extreme tightness vs. EU gas+storage deficit
Geopolitical LNG supply risk (Hormuz, sanctions clarity)
Storage refill dynamics under high power+gas demand
Coal historically depressed (7th pctile); gas in-the-money vs. thermal
top_drivers: GB power structural tightness (98th pctile, 155 EUR/MWh) on island supply constraints vs. continent; renewable share volatile week-on-week (+28.6%), indicating weather sensitivity.

Geopolitical LNG premium from Middle East Hormuz risk and EU sanctions clarity; TTF at 73rd pctile (61.9 EUR/MWh) trading extended 2.5σ above 50d trend—arbitrage window supports inflows, but storage 15.7pp below seasonal limits upside if demand remains elevated.

Coal at 7th pctile historically cheap (96 USD/t, stale 210d); clean spark at 89th pctile (31.85 EUR/MWh) confirms gas firmly in-the-money for marginal generation—supports TTF bid and limits coal dispatch upside.
top_takeaway: GB power at 98th percentile (155 EUR/MWh) on tight supply; storage 16pp below seasonal; Hormuz risk and EU sanctions clarity lift TTF—watch refill pace and LNG arbitrage.

watchlist.why: GB at 98th pctile vs. DE at 83rd; structural island tightness (wind, interconnect, thermal) vs. continental solar+nuclear buffer. 155 EUR/MWh unsustainable if demand softens or interconnect maintenance ends.

Hormuz instability raising Asian spot premiums; EU storage 15.7pp below seasonal means high-cost infill critical. TTF at 73rd pctile (61.9 EUR/MWh, +14.6% weekly); arbitrage window open if Asia LNG spikes further.
28th pctile fill rate (54.6%) at critical juncture. High power+gas prices depress demand; EU sanctions deal may stabilize Russian supply expectations, lowering refill urgency premium.
Outlier daily selloff at 34.17 EUR/tCO2 (47th pctile). German nuclear approval bearish-power may be weighing; monitor if DB spreads widen further, lowering marginal-cost dispatch and EUA floor.

High wind+solar is suppressing DA pricing in EU; yet GB remains tight, indicating regional decoupling. If renewable forecast swings negative (low wind week ahead), GB premium could spike; DA-QH spread widens.

watchlist_dated.name: EU sanctions implementation timeline
watchlist_dated.why: Politico report—Greek concession clinches deal. Timetable for Russian gas reroute logistics and third-country flow diversion will reset LNG arb expectations and TTF medium-term curve shape.
